The scrape-off layer is the interface between the hot plasma core and cold material surfaces that must be protected.
Filamentary motion refers to the radial propagation of coherent structures, commonly termed blobs or filaments, in the scrape-off layer.
The Militello-Omotani (MO) model is a statistical description of filamentary motion that relates spatial profiles in the scrape-off layer to the dynamics of filaments.

The stochastic framework used in this paper is based on the MO model and uses a one-dimensional (radial) density signal constructed by the superposition of statistically distributed pulses with a given spatial waveform.
The filament ejection rate is given by f = N /∆t, where N is the total number of filaments ejected and ∆t is the time interval.
The sink timescale is the time-scale of the source/sink, which can depend on spatial position or time.
The filament velocity relation is given by v = v v˜(x,t)η1/2, where v is a scaling parameter for the velocity and v˜(x,t) contains any spatial and temporal dependance of the filament velocity.
The amplitude distribution function is an exponential function, P(η) = exp(-η/η∗), where η∗ is the e-folding amplitude.
The width distribution function is a log-normal function, P(δ) = (1/√(2πσ^2)) exp(-(ln(δ)-ln(δ))^2/(2σ^2)), where δ is the most probable value of δ and σ is the spread parameter.
The baseline simulation is a simulation that matches the experimental measurements early in the density ramps.
The localized reduction in the density sink is a reduction in the density sink acting on the filaments within the model, which occurs over a highly localized region.
The filament acceleration is a change in the velocity of the filaments, which is necessary to explain the expansion and flattening of the shoulder region.
The simulation time is 1.8 s, and the number of samples in ∆t is 600,000.
The filament ejection rate is 1.5 × 10^5 s^-1.
